newsitem.title: UK: LIBERTY SEES STRONG PERFORMANCE THIS YEAR.
newsitem.headline: LIBERTY SEES STRONG PERFORMANCE THIS YEAR.

text.p: Property to financial services group Liberty International Holdings said on Thursday it should produce a strong performance this year unless conditions change markedly in the UK shopping centre and commercial property market.

The upbeat statement accompanied news of a 10 percent increase in first half pretax profits to 61.8 million stg. The company, which is 69 percent-owned by South African insurance giant Liberty Life Insurance Ltd, also raised its interim dividend 10 percent to 8.00p per share.

"With a fully income producing and well located shopping centre and commercial property portfolio, a low level of gearing and significant cash balances we are well insulated against a deteriorating economic picture," said chairman Donald Gordon.
Liberty's first half operating profit was driven by strong growth in shopping centre rental income, which rose to 45.3 million stg from 38.2 million.
Profits were also boosted by a six million stg trading profit on the sale of Albany Place, Welwyn by Capital and Counties.
Liberty's financial services showed a small operating loss of 3.7 million from a gain of 200,000 previously and the company does not expect to see meaningful profitability here for a number of years.

Liberty said that an external valuation of property company Capital Shopping Centres (CSC), in which it owns 72 percent, produced a gross valuation of 1.65 billion stg at June 30 from 1.51 billion at December 31, 1996. It floated CSC as a separate company in 1996.
Some 97 million stg of the revaluation surplus of 135 million stg is attributable to shareholders and helped boost the company's net asset value to 473p per share from 436p per share previously.
